text: The short-term holder cluster under $BTC has failed to hold. As price broke below the $62K–$65K block, short-term holders started ramping up their selling at a loss. Cost basis clusters like this often become resistance once price is below them.

Whales trading on Hyperliquid are short $BTC. Aside from a brief flip to long last week, they have been net short since the beginning of November. They stayed short into this morning's new low, though the position has shrunk slightly.

The largest $BTC liquidation cluster has been cleared. We have been tracking a dense cluster of long liquidations between $59K and $62K for months. Yesterday, they were fully cleared out, removing a large source of forced selling under price.

The average Bitcoin holder is still in profit. $BTC trades above its realized price, the average cost of every coin on the network. The margin is thin: MVRV sits just above 1. A break below would put holders in loss for the first time since early 2023.

Crypto futures correctly flagged the $ANT IPO price as too low. All week they valued Anthropic above $1.7 trillion, while the IPO was set at $1.5 trillion. In the hour before the open, crypto futures rallied to $2T, right where Nasdaq's first trade landed.

Anthropic set a pre-IPO trading record. $9.5B was traded in Anthropic futures on crypto venues before today's Nasdaq debut. SpaceX, the largest IPO on record, drew $3.9B before its June listing. Pre-IPO price discovery now happens on crypto rails.
